summary: Hotfix assist: session stabilization and safe optimizer retraction for tenant experiencing tail latencies
description:
Issue summary:
BrightPost Health reported repeated multi-minute tail latency spikes for a small subset (~2%) of long-lived chat sessions after the customer enabled a mixed-precision quantization profile "mp-q-low" and async batching increments. Impact is visible as degraded 95/99p response times and several streaming disconnects during multi-turn conversations.

Impact:
- Affected tenant: BrightPost Health (dedicated pool).
- Symptom window: 2026-03-09 21:00 to 2026-03-10 03:00 UTC.
- Business impact: production user-facing degraded throughput and periodic request timeouts for clinical-assist flows (non-blocking but disruptive).

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated (dedicated GPU pool) in prod:us-east-1.
- Serving runtime: 2.7.1-hotfix-candidate (custom flags for tenant).
- Tenant had enabled: mixed-precision quant profile "mp-q-low" + async interleaved batching with kv-prefetch enabled.
- Models in traffic: redwood-open-7b (primary), fallback to llama2-13b for long-context cases.

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Rehydrate long chat session ( > 80 tokens prefix) with sustained multi-turn traffic.
2) Enable aggressive async-batch window (max_batch_delay=25ms) and kv-prefetch on the tenant profile.
3) Send sequences with varied token-lengths (mix of 16 - 400 tokens); observe high variance in seq length.
4) Observe tail latency and occasional 5xx streaming disconnects on metrics dashboards (trace IDs in logs).

Observed behavior:
- 95p/99p latency regressed by ~3x for affected sessions.
- KV-cache eviction spikes correlated with quantized-kv layout changes leading to cache-miss storms for long sessions.
- Scheduler interleaving sometimes combined async batches from high and low priority sessions, causing head-of-line blocking.
- Streaming connections intermittently closed with upstream code 502 followed by retry that sometimes succeeds.

Expected behavior:
- Stable 95p latency within SLA for dedicated tenant, graceful degradation if under memory pressure, and no streaming disconnects during normal throughput.

Logs / metrics references:
- Grafana tail-latency dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/latency/tenant-brightpost?from=2026-03-09T20:00:00Z&to=2026-03-10T04:00:00Z
- SRE tracing span: trace-redwood-77a3dc (example traces attached in ticket).
- Serving runtime logs: /var/logs/runner/brightpost/2026-03-09.log (error windows annotated).

Initial workaround provided to customer:
- We suggested a temporary traffic-split by session age: route sessions older than 30s to a conservative profile (disable async batching and set quant profile to "fp16-safe").
- Applied immediate tenant flag to reduce async batch window to 5ms and disabled kv-prefetch for their tenant pool at 2026-03-10T00:12 UTC.

Request from customer:
- Assistance to safely retract the mixed-precision quant profile and async batching without causing mass cache thrash or CPU/GPU thrashing in the dedicated pool.
- Desire for minimal user-visible disruption and a short maintenance window if needed.
comments: Aditi Mehta (Support) - 2026-03-10: Received initial report from BrightPost Health via support channel. Customer reports 95p latency jumps and some streaming disconnects. Asked for tenant flags and sample trace IDs.
BrightPost Health - 2026-03-10: Provided traces trace-redwood-77a3dc, trace-redwood-88b7ab, and confirmed enabling of mp-q-low + async batching last night as part of a cost-optimization experiment.

Riley Thompson (SRE) - 2026-03-10: Scoped to dedicated pool; started live telemetry review. Observed synchronized KV-cache evictions and a correlating spike in GPU memory pressure when mixed-precision evictions occurred.

Carlos Nguyen (Runtime Eng) - 2026-03-11: Proposed two-step safe retraction: 1) session-level gating to pin active sessions to conservative profile; 2) staged demote of tenant profile with snapshot restore of previous kv-layout. Preparing PR for safe-demote tooling.
Support (Aditi) - 2026-03-11: Customer agreed to a short maintenance window; requested clear rollback / recover plan in case of regressions.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: Mixed-precision quant profile changed memory layout for kv entries, increasing miss penalty during cache rehydration. Combined with async interleaved batching, long sessions experienced head-of-line blocking.
Confirmed correlation between kv-eviction spikes and tail-latency windows using internal eviction metrics (evict-rate metric filter matched timing).
Observed that disabling kv-prefetch reduced miss-rate but increased cold-start latency modestly; this tradeoff acceptable for affected tenant given user impact.
Scheduler logs show occasional merging of small batches from unrelated sessions due to aggressive window. Introducing session-affinity for batching prevents mixing of long and short sessions.
Prepared a hotpatch (PR #5123) that exposes a session-gate flag and a tenant-safe-demote operation which replays a stored kv-snapshot rather than cold-evicting on profile change.
resolution:
Workaround and staged fix applied: 1) Immediate mitigation executed 2026-03-10T00:12 UTC - reduced async batch window to 5ms and disabled kv-prefetch for BrightPost tenant. This lowered 99p latency ~45% for affected sessions. 2) 2026-03-11 02:30 UTC - applied session-stabilization hotpatch (runtime PR #5123) in a canary subset (10% traffic) with session-affinity enforced for batching and a safe-demote path that restores kv-layout from snapshot before completing quant-profile change. Canary metrics show stable tail-latency and no additional streaming disconnects. 3) 2026-03-11 04:00 UTC - rolled to 100% tenant traffic after validation.

Follow-ups / Action items:
- Postmortem: schedule for 2026-03-16 to document root cause and long-term mitigations (owner: Riley Thompson).
- Add an automated canary check when applying quant-profile changes that validates kv-eviction delta and tail-latency for a shadowed session group. (owner: Carlos Nguyen)
post_resolution_tasks: Create a runbook snippet for session-gated profile changes and safe-demote (assigned Riley).
Instrument a health-check that rejects quant-profile rollouts if eviction-rate delta > 2x for baseline window.
Customer follow-up call scheduled: 2026-03-12 15:00 UTC to review changes and confirm SLA expectations.
